passage:
Note from Chandrika, class teacher.
At the games period, Ira and another child argued over whether a marble touched the line. "It did!" "It didn't!" Each said it louder, each repeated the same words, and the circle of onlookers grew. Ira's fists were clenched, and neither was listening. I stepped in and said, "Ira, before you answer, tell me what the other person just said." Ira stared, then said, "That it didn't touch. Because it stopped early." I asked the other child the same. They were quiet for a moment. Then Ira said, "Okay. Let's look at the line together." I will try this again next week.

qa.q: What did the children argue about?
qa.a: Whether a marble touched the line.

qa.q: What was Ira wanting during the argument, judging by the clenched fists and the loud repeats?
qa.a: Angry and set on winning, with clenched fists and loud repeats, rather than trying to understand the other child.

qa.q: What did Chandrika suggest that started to change the pattern?
qa.a: Chandrika asked Ira to say what the other person had just said before answering.

qa.q: How might the other child have felt when Ira repeated the point about the marble stopping early?
qa.a: Heard and a bit surprised, since the other point was said aloud and the shouting stopped, making it easier to look at the line together.

grounding: Children arguing over a game push louder and repeat the same claim; stating what the other said before answering begins to change the pattern.

passage:
Sunday night. Today Salma and I had a big fight in the carrom game. I said the coin was in the pocket, Salma said it wasn't, and we both got louder and louder, until Mummy came and said, "Karthik, tell Salma what she said, before you say your thing." I was so cross. But I tried. "You said the coin didn't go in because it touched the edge." Salma's face changed. "Yes! You heard me." Then she said, "You said it went in because the edge is soft?" "Yes." It was so strange. We looked at the board together, and there was a little dent. We both laughed.
Karthik

qa.q: What game did Karthik and Salma play?
What was Karthik feeling when Mummy said to repeat what Salma said?
qa.a: Cross, though Karthik tried anyway. Wanting to win made it hard to listen at first.

qa.q: What did Karthik do that changed the fight?
qa.a: Karthik said back what Salma had said before giving Karthik's own view, and then they looked at the board together.

qa.q: How might Salma have felt when Karthik repeated what she said?
qa.a: Heard and happier, since her face changed and she said "You heard me," then repeated Karthik's view in turn.

grounding: Children arguing over a game push louder; stating what the other person said before answering changes the pattern.
